newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks jump 2.78 pct in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks jump 2.78 pct in high volume.

text.p: The Athens bourse ended 2.78 percent higher on heavy volume with market watchers saying the market had warmed up to positive economic news for Greece such as Moody's recent credit upgrading and easing inflation and interest rates.

"We have entered a period of superior bourse performance, due to Greece's recent upgrading by Moody's and news of declining inflation and interest rates. Monday's strong session reflected these good news," said John Haveles, an investment analyst at Delphi Mutual Funds.
A correction within the next few days could take place, he said.
"I wish a market correction occurs soon because in the past strong market rises brought about abrupt corrections. After a market correction, the market will become more stable," he added.
More capital is flowing into growth funds and these, in turn, are investing more heavily than before in stocks, he added.
The Athens general share index jumped 2.78 percent or 30.09 points at 1113.91 from Friday's 1083.82, after opening at 1086.89.

"Greek and foreign institutionals continue to show a strong buying interest in the Greek bourse. The banking sector is particularly attractive," said broker Dimitris Matsaganis at National Securities.
Shares of National Bank performed strongly on Monday on news of a bonus distribution, Matsaganis added.
Banks gained 4.24 percent, construction rose 2.05 percent and investment shares gained 2.54 percent.
Monday's turnover was 15.3 billion drachmas on volume of 5.5 million shares. Gainers led losers 158 to 75 with 24 issues unchanged on 257 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 899.00-917.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, gained 90 drachmas to close at 5,390.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $17.52-$18.52. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 7,180-7,604 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
